<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XII.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|31}}</noinclude>lawful for them to doe on the Sabboth-dayes. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=3}}† But he sayd to them, Haue you not read vvhat {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Re. 21, 4.''}}* Dauid did vvhen he vvas an hungred, and they that vvere vvith him: {{verse|chapter=12|verse=4}}† hovv he entred into the house of God, and did eate the loaues of proposition, vvhich it vvas not lavvful for him to eate, nor for them that vvere with him, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 24, 9.''}}* but for priestes only? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=5}}† Or haue ye not read in the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Nu. 28, 9.''}}* Lavv, that on Sabboth-dayes the priestes in the temple do breake the Sabboth, and are vvithout blame? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=6}}† but I tel you that there is here a greater then the tēple. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=7}}† And if you did knovv vvhat it is, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ose. 6, 6.''}}* ''I wil mercie, and not '' {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the annotatiō chap. ''9, 13.''}}∷ ''sacrifice'': you vvould neuer haue condemned the innocentes. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=8}}† For the Sonne of man is lord of the Sabboth also.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=9}}† And vvhen he had passed from thence, he came into their synagogue. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=10}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 3, 1. Lu. 6, 6.''}}* behold there vvas a man vvhich had a vvithered hand, and they asked him saying, Whether is it lavvful to cure on the Sabboths? that they might accuse him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=11}}† But he sayd to them, what man shal there be of you, that shal haue one sheepe: and if the same fall into a ditche on the Sabboths, vvil he not take hold and lift it vp? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=12}}† Hovv much better is a man more then a sheepe? therfore it is lavvful on the Sabboths to doe a good deede. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=13}}† Then he sayth to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. and he stretched it forth, and it vvas restored to health euen as the other.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=14}}† And the Pharisees going forth made a consultation agaynst him, how they might destroy him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=15}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving it, retired from thence: and many folovved him, and he cured them all. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=16}}† and he charged them that they should not disclose him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=17}}† That it might be fulfilled vvhich vvas spoken by Esay the Prophete, saying. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=18}}† ''Behold my seruant vvhom I haue chosen, my beloued in vvhom my soul hath vvel liked. I vvil put my spirit vpon him, and iudgement to the Gentiles shal he shew''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Es. 42, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=12|verse=19}}† ''He shal not contend, nor crie out, neither shal any man heare in the streetes his voyce''. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=20}}† ''The reede bruised he shal not breake, and smoking flaxe he shal not extinguish: til he cast forth iudgement vnto victorie''. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=21}}† ''And in his name the Gentiles shal hope''.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=22}}† Then {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 11, 14. Mar. 3, 22.''}}* vvas offered to him one possessed vvith a deuil, blinde and dumme: and he cured him, so that he spake & saw. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=23}}† And al the multitudes vvere amased, and sayd, Whether this be the Sonne of Dauid? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=24}}† But the Pharisees hearing it, sayd. This felovv casteth not out diuels but {{sup|‖}} in Beelzebub the Prince of the diuels. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=25}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving their cogitations, said to them.

Euery kingdom {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Therfore the kingdom of heretikes can not possibly stand, because it is alwayes ful of diuisiō and dissension.}}∷ deuided against it self shal be made<noinclude>{{rh|||desolate:}}</noinclude>
